sourceTree.pathsRelativeTo: the upstream repository root. A provenance path of "firmware/sesame-firmware-main.ino" therefore resolves to firmware/upstream/firmware/sesame-firmware-main.ino, the tree pinned at meta.sourceTree.upstreamCommit. F2 has since run, so that is the citable location; the gitignored reference/sesame-robot-main/ snapshot F4 originally read is byte-identical to it (129/129 files) but is absent from a clean clone. pnpm validate:hardware-map --check-lines verifies every citation's line number against firmware/upstream/.

F4 read the vendored reference/sesame-robot-main/ snapshot, which F2 verified byte-for-byte identical to firmware/upstream/ at this commit for all 129 files (docs/findings/F2-upstream-drift.md), so every provenance citation in this file resolves against this commit. meta.verifiedFlagPolicy: Every fact in this file was read directly out of firmware source unless it carries an explicit "*Verified": false (or a "*Note" naming a non-source origin such as firmware/README.md). Absence of a verified flag means "extracted from source at the cited file:line". Facts that could not be established from source are null AND listed in `unresolved` — they are never guessed. Anything sourced only from documentation is marked unverified because F4 also found the documentation to be wrong in several places (see docs/findings/F4-doc-drift.md).
meta.provenanceContract: Every extracted fact carries a `source` (or `*Source`) object of the form {"file": "<path relative to the upstream repo root>", "line": <1-based line number>}. A fact without provenance is a bug. ONE EXCEPTION, added 2026-08-24 by the Q3 LEDC corrections: a handful of servo facts are properties of the ESP32Servo LIBRARY rather than of Sesame's own source, and the library lives under the gitignored tools/ tree. Those carry a `librarySource`-shaped object — {library, version, file (relative to the LIBRARY root), line, text, versionPin, obtainWith, installedAtNote} — which is deliberately not two-key {file,line} so `pnpm validate:hardware-map --check-lines` does not try to resolve it against the firmware tree. The citable identity is library+version+path+line, which survives a clean clone; the machine-local install path is recorded in installedAtNote only.

servos.orderNote: ORDERED ARRAY, firmware enum order — deliberately NOT geometric and NOT alphabetical. enum ServoName { R1=0, R2=1, L1=2, L2=3, R4=4, R3=5, L3=6, L4=7 }. Never re-sort.

servoConfig.libraryVersionNote: Version is a README recommendation, not encoded in source. No library.properties / sketch profile is checked in.
servoConfig.pwmTimersProgrammedNote: MEASURED, not read from firmware source: only HSTIMER0 and LSTIMER0 — one per LEDC speed group — are ever written. arduino-esp32 3.3.11's find_matching_timer() reuses a hardware timer whenever frequency AND resolution match within a speed group, and all eight servos are 50 Hz / 10-bit, so each group collapses onto its own timer 0. pwmTimersAllocated above is a correct record of the four allocateTimer() CALLS; two of the four reservations have no hardware effect. Source: docs/findings/Q3-ledc-fidelity.md §2.3, §6.3 (LEDC register file read back over QEMU's gdbstub).
servoConfig.ledcSpeedGroupNote: MEASURED, not read from firmware source: the eight servos occupy BOTH LEDC speed groups, four channels each — not one group of eight. ESP32PWM::timerAndIndexToChannel() hands out channels {0,1,8,9} for its timer 0 and {2,3,10,11} for its timer 1; arduino-esp32 3.3.11 esp32-hal-ledc.c:222 maps group = channel / SOC_LEDC_CHANNEL_NUM, so 0-7 are high-speed and 8-15 low-speed. Exactly these eight CONF0 registers read back non-zero, and the four LS ones carry the LS-only PARA_UP bit. Original ESP32 only: the S2/S3 have no high-speed group. Source: docs/findings/Q3-ledc-fidelity.md §2.3.

clampSource.installedAtNote: tools/arduino-data/data/internal/ESP32Servo_3.0.9_442075ee231ab4b5/ESP32Servo/src/ESP32Servo.cpp on this machine; gitignored, cite by library+version+line.

attachPulseClamp.note: BOTH FACTS ARE TRUE AND THEY DIFFER. The firmware really does call attach(pin, 732, 2929) at sesame-firmware-main.ino:742 — attachMaxPulseRequestedUs and attachCall record that verbatim. ESP32Servo::attach() then clamps the requested max to MAX_PULSE_WIDTH before storing it, so the widest pulse the peripheral is ever asked for is 2500 us — attachMaxPulseUs records THAT, because it is the number every angle-to-pulse calculation must use. The minimum is NOT clamped (732 > MIN_PULSE_WIDTH 500), which is why only the top end moved. Confirmed independently by measurement: 180 deg produced 12% duty at a 20 ms frame = 2500 us; 2929 us would have been 14.6%. Source: docs/findings/Q3-ledc-fidelity.md §3, §6.2.

resolutionSource.text: #define DEFAULT_TIMER_WIDTH 10   (the #else branch; the ARDUINO_ESP32C3_DEV branch at :87 also defines 10, so the value is 10 either way)
resolutionSource.installedAtNote: tools/arduino-data/data/internal/ESP32Servo_3.0.9_442075ee231ab4b5/ESP32Servo/src/ESP32Servo.h on this machine; gitignored, cite by library+version+line. Confirmed at runtime: the LEDC timer config register read back duty_res = 10 (Q3 §2.1).

tickConversionSource.text: int Servo::usToTicks(int usec) — usec / (REFRESH_USEC / timer_width_ticks) = usec / (20000 / 1024), truncated to int
tickConversionSource.installedAtNote: tools/arduino-data/data/internal/ESP32Servo_3.0.9_442075ee231ab4b5/ESP32Servo/src/ESP32Servo.cpp on this machine; gitignored, cite by library+version+line.

pulseQuantisation.note: THE SERVO CHANNELS ARE 10-BIT, SO COMMANDED ANGLES ALIAS. Servo::write() maps 0..180 onto 732..2500 us with Arduino integer map(), then usToTicks() truncates to a 1024-step, 20 ms frame. Only ticks 37..128 are reachable across the whole 0..180 range: 92 distinct pulse values for 181 distinct commands, so 89 of the 181 angles produce a pulse identical to a neighbour's at the pin. This is a property of REAL HARDWARE, not a QEMU artefact — anything in the UI or the simulator implying 1 deg of servo resolution is over-claiming. Derived by enumerating all 181 angles through the library's own arithmetic (Q3 §6.4, re-derived independently here); helper: quantiseCommandedAngle() in @sesame-lab/sesame-model. Source: docs/findings/Q3-ledc-fidelity.md §6.4.

motorCurrentDelay.purposeComment: ms delay between motor movements to prevent over-current
motorCurrentDelay.appliedNote: NOT a bare delay(): delayWithFace() spins for the duration while servicing updateAnimatedFace(), server.handleClient() and dnsServer.processNextRequest() with a delay(5) per iteration. Every setServoAngle() therefore also pumps the HTTP/DNS/face subsystems.

subtrim.mechanism: per-channel signed degree offset added before clamping
subtrim.persistedNote: RAM only. `subtrim save` (serial) prints a C initialiser for the user to paste back into source; nothing is written to NVS/flash.

steps.description: Guard: if (channel < 8). Channels >= 8 are silently ignored — no error, no clamp, no write.
adjustedAngle = constrain(angle + servoSubtrim[channel], 0, 180). Subtrim is added BEFORE the clamp, so a large subtrim can saturate the output.

servos[channel].write(adjustedAngle) — ESP32Servo maps 0..180 deg onto the EFFECTIVE 732..2500 us pulse range, then quantises it to 10-bit LEDC ticks. attach() requested 732..2929 but the library clamped the max to MAX_PULSE_WIDTH 2500; see servoConfig.attachPulseClamp and servoConfig.pulseQuantisation.
delayWithFace(motorCurrentDelay) — cooperative stagger delay that also services face animation, HTTP and DNS.

setServoAngle.positionFeedbackNote: The stock robot has no joint-position feedback. setServoAngle() is write-only; nothing reads servo state back. Any "measured angle" in a simulator must be null.

convergencePoint.note: Single convergence point for all servo motion: every movement function, the serial CLI and /cmd?motor= all funnel through setServoAngle(). This is the one hook site an instrumentation patch needs (R6).

display.resetPinNote: OLED_RESET -1 = share the MCU reset / no dedicated reset line.
display.busClockNote: Never set in source — there is no Wire.setClock() call anywhere in the firmware, so the bus runs at the Arduino-ESP32 default. firmware/README.md:164 claims 400 kHz Fast Mode; that claim is NOT supported by the source. Recorded as null.
display.bootFailureBehaviour: hard-fail: prints an error then spins forever in a bare while(1) — setup() never returns, loop() never runs, the watchdog is the only escape.
display.bootFailureImplication: Unmodified firmware cannot boot past setup() in an emulator that does not answer the SSD1306 on I2C 0x3C. Either an I2C/SSD1306 model or a build-time patch is required before any post-display milestone (WiFi, web server, servo attach) can be reached.

ap.defaultIpNote: Not hard-coded in source — the firmware reads WiFi.softAPIP() at runtime (line 689). 192.168.4.1 is the Arduino-ESP32 SoftAP default and is only asserted by firmware/README.md:192.
ap.channelNote: Not configured in source; the 2-argument WiFi.softAP() overload is used, so core defaults apply.

dns.purpose: captive portal — every DNS query is answered with the SoftAP IP

routes.description: Serves the captive-portal control UI (index_html, a PROGMEM raw string literal).

Legacy query-parameter command endpoint. Accepts exactly one of: pose=<name>, go=<dir>, stop=<any>, or motor=<1-8|R1..L4>&value=<0-180>. Responds 200 "OK" immediately (before the movement runs); 400 "Invalid motor or angle" or 400 "Bad Args" otherwise.
Updates frameDelay, walkCycles, motorCurrentDelay and faceFps from query args (each optional). faceFps is floored at 1. No range validation on the other three. Responds 200 "OK".
JSON status: currentCommand, currentFace, networkConnected, apIP, and networkIP only when connected.

JSON command endpoint. Registered for ANY method but the handler rejects non-POST with 405. Body is parsed with manual indexOf/substring string scanning (no JSON library) against server.arg("plain"). Supports {"command":...}, {"face":...}, or both; a body with a face and no "command" key is treated as face-only.
Async WiFi scan. Returns {"scanning":true} while a scan is running or being started, otherwise a JSON array of {ssid,rssi,secure}. Brings the STA interface up if needed and drops it again afterwards.
Queues a non-blocking station join (form args ssid, password). 405 on non-POST, 400 on empty ssid, 409 if an attempt is already in flight, otherwise 200 {"success":true,"pending":true}.
Station state for the Settings panel: connected, connecting, lastError, and on success ssid/ip/host/mdns/rssi.
Catch-all registered via server.onNotFound(). Paths starting with /api/ get a JSON 404; every other unmatched path is served the portal HTML (captive-portal redirect behaviour).

http.routeRegistrationNote: Every route is registered with the two-argument WebServer::on(uri, handler) overload, which binds HTTP_ANY. Method restrictions exist only inside handlers (/api/command and /api/wifi/connect return 405 for non-POST). GET-only documentation in firmware/README.md is therefore not enforced by the server.

faces.bitmapDataNote: Pixel data intentionally not extracted. Each face bitmap is a 1024-byte horizontal-scan PROGMEM array named epd_bitmap_<face>[] (frames epd_bitmap_<face>_1..._5); the per-face `frames[].source` gives the exact definition line.

playbackModes.behaviour: advance to the last frame, then set faceAnimFinished and stop
ping-pong: advance to the last frame, reverse direction, run back to 0, reverse again

faces.playbackModeOwnership: Playback mode is NOT a property of a face. It is global state (currentFaceMode, ino:58, initialised to FACE_ANIM_LOOP) set per call site by setFaceWithMode(). setFace() alone does not change it. Each face therefore records the modes observed at its call sites, not a declared mode.
faces.fpsRuntimeSettable: GET /setSettings?faceFps=<int>, floored at 1 (ino:284) — only affects faces absent from faceFpsEntries[]

idle.entryCondition: runStandPose(face == 1) calls enterIdle(). That is the ONLY call site.
idle.entryConditionNote: Idle is entered on completion of a stand pose, NOT after a period of inactivity. firmware/README.md:667 claims inactivity-based entry; the source does not implement that.
idle.exitCondition: exitIdle() from /cmd?pose=, /cmd?go=, or POST /api/command with a non-stop command

All four LEDC timers reserved before any attach(). Only two are ever programmed — HSTIMER0 and LSTIMER0, one per speed group — because all eight servos share 50 Hz / 10-bit (servoConfig.pwmTimersProgrammed).

Servo attach happens LAST of the peripherals — after WiFi and the web server, not before. The 2929 in `operation` is the value the CALL passes; ESP32Servo clamps it to 2500 us inside attach(), so the effective window is 732..2500 (servoConfig.attachPulseClamp).
Bare delay(); the only one in setup().
Deliberately shows a face without moving motors. currentFaceMode is still its initial FACE_ANIM_LOOP (ino:58) because setFace() does not change the mode.
Last statement of setup(); a good "boot complete" marker for a Renode probe.

commands.dispatchNote: loop() re-evaluates currentCommand on EVERY iteration. Movement functions that do not clear it (forward/backward/left/right) therefore repeat until something else clears it; pose functions clear it themselves via `if (currentCommand == "<name>") currentCommand = "";`. A command string that matches no branch is never cleared and simply does nothing forever.

vocabulary.clearsSelfNote: cleared inline in loop(), not inside the pose function
cleared inline in loop(), not inside the pose function

vocabulary.note: Not a loop() branch — handled at the HTTP layer by assigning currentCommand = "".
Idle sentinel. The empty string is the "no command" state; loop() skips the dispatch block entirely.

setServoAngle(motor, angle) for motor 0-7 (no angle range check here — setServoAngle clamps)

commands.serialCliDispatchNote: Serial CLI matching is prefix-order-sensitive: `strcmp("subtrim save")` is tested at line 833 AFTER the exact `strcmp("subtrim")` at 825 but BEFORE the `strncmp("subtrim ", 8)` at 846, and the `st ` abbreviation is disambiguated by inspecting command_buffer[1]. `strncmp(command_buffer, "st ", 3)` at line 846 also matches "st save"/"st reset" prefixes, which are caught earlier.

unresolved.subject: boards[distro-v2].i2c
unresolved.reason: There is no V2-specific I2C block in source. The single commented block at firmware/sesame-firmware-main.ino:30-32 is labelled "I2C Pins for Distro Board V2 / V3" and covers both. Recorded as 8/9 on that basis; firmware/README.md:778-779 agrees. Not independently confirmed against the V2 schematic.

unresolved.subject: boards[*].mcuFamily
unresolved.reason: The .ino never names an MCU family; the pin arrays are just integers. Families are taken from firmware/README.md (flashing board selection at :60-62 and HAL table headings at :721/:736/:751/:766) and are marked mcuFamilyVerified: false. Confirming them requires the PCB schematics under hardware/pcb/ or an arduino-cli build (F3).

unresolved.subject: display.busClockHz
unresolved.reason: No Wire.setClock() call exists anywhere in the firmware, so the bus runs at the Arduino-ESP32 core default. firmware/README.md:164 asserts 400 kHz Fast Mode; that is unsupported by source. Left null rather than guessing the core default, which is core-version dependent.

unresolved.subject: network.ap.defaultIp
unresolved.reason: Read at runtime via WiFi.softAPIP() (ino:689); never hard-coded. 192.168.4.1 is the Arduino-ESP32 SoftAP default and is only asserted by firmware/README.md:192. Marked defaultIpVerified: false.

unresolved.subject: servos.servoConfig.libraryVersionPinned and the Adafruit libraries
unresolved.reason: No sketch profile, library.properties or lockfile is checked in upstream. ESP32Servo 3.0.9 is a README recommendation (firmware/README.md:42, :175); Adafruit_SSD1306 and Adafruit_GFX carry no version at all. F3 owns pinning these.

unresolved.subject: faces.faces[*].playbackModes
unresolved.reason: Playback mode is global state (currentFaceMode), not a face attribute. 19 of the 38 registered faces — every conversational face plus "defualt"/"default" — are never passed to setFaceWithMode() anywhere in firmware, so they have no intrinsic mode. Their entries carry an empty playbackModes array and a playbackModeNote.

unresolved.subject: servos.servoConfig — physical servo model, torque, slew rate
unresolved.reason: Not in firmware. The BOM (hardware/bom/README.md) names MG90S 180-degree metal-gear micro servos, but no rate/torque data exists anywhere in this repository. Any simulated slew rate in Phase 1 must be declared "inferred", not "observed".

unresolved.subject: servos.joints[*] — axis, zero reference, direction sign, semantic name
unresolved.reason: Deliberately out of F4 scope and absent from firmware: the enum names R1..L4 carry no geometry. F5/F6 derive this from the STL/CAD. Nothing in this file may be read as a claim about which physical leg a joint drives.

unresolved.subject: commands.vocabulary
unresolved.reason: A currentCommand value that matches no branch in the loop() if/else chain (ino:762-783) is never cleared and never dispatched — the robot silently does nothing until another command arrives. There is no error path and no enumeration of "valid" commands in source, so the vocabulary here is the set of strings the dispatcher recognises, not a validated allowlist.

unresolved.subject: faces.faces[stand], faces.faces[defualt], faces.faces[default], faces.faces[thinking]
unresolved.reason: epd_bitmap_stand and epd_bitmap_defualt are declared as weak symbols (face-bitmaps.h:52) but never defined, so those faces have 0 frames and render nothing — including the global fallback face. epd_bitmap_thinking_2 is defined without a preceding _1, so it is unreachable. This is upstream behaviour, faithfully recorded, not a transcription error.
